messages.subject: inla in user defined function
parts:

"Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'depvar' not found"

According to R-logic such a task should be possible. Is there a working example? 

Kind regards

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla in user defined function
parts:
On Fri, 2016-10-07 at 01:21 -0700, oeyh...@gmail.com wrote:
> mandag 3. oktober 2016 22.42.11 UTC+2 skrev Havard Rue følgende:
> > On Mon, 2016-10-03 at 13:36 -0700, oeyh...@gmail.com wrote: 
> > > I would like to run the same inla model with plots of results
> > for 
> > > several data sets, and  in order to give the commands only once,
> > I 
> > > have created an R function calling inla. I have not been able to
> >

do like this instead, and add 'y' into the data.frame, which is a copy
in any case

    data$y = data[, yName]
    mod.inla.yName = inla(data = data, formula = y ~ time, family =
"normal")


PS: your 'y2' is so badly scaled that inla fail to fit it due to
overflow.... 

H

Given the requirements of the INLA-function, that each entry of the formula need be contained in the data frame (or list), the basic trick is to construct a frame/list with standard names to be used by INLA. The task of the outer function is simply to translate other names to standard ones, and to keep track of the translations.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla in user defined function
parts:
Hi,
That code is slightly unsafe. Imagine for example having xName="y" and yName="x". To be safe, you need to build a separate copy of the "data" collection, or rebuild the whole structure in a single construction that replace the entire collection at once:
data <- data.frame(x=data[,xName], y=data[,yName])

Finn
